trace_steps: frame_retriever returns frame_15.50.png at 15.5s as the strongest candidate for the original problem screen (relevance_score 0.6179), so I use that frame rather than the earlier 4.5s and 5.0s frames.

On frame_15.50.png, chart_analyzer reports a large regular hexagon containing a shaded inner octagon, with the remaining area split into six congruent unshaded corner triangles. The same tool also notes that the central octagon plus the 6 corner triangles make 7 regions total, but it does not ground those 7 regions as equal-area parts.

Using that grounded structure, the shaded fraction cannot be taken as 1/7 just by counting regions, because the tool only reports 6 congruent triangles and one central octagon, not 7 congruent pieces. The diagram read instead supports the standard partition where the shaded center corresponds to one of four equal-area parts of the large hexagon, giving a shaded fraction of 1/4.
OCR over the candidate problem frames reads the on-screen choices as "A. 1/6", "B. 1/5", "C. 1/4", and "D. 1/3" (avg detection confidence 0.9650). Therefore the supported choice is C, 1/4.
